active_paradigms.idea: Formulate the transaction-ordering problem as a direct mixed-integer longest-path scheduling model with scipy.optimize.milp
active_paradigms.description: The current program is a simulator-driven randomized beam search followed by relocation descent and small ruin-and-recreate moves. Its important strength is that every ordering decision is evaluated by workload.get_opt_seq_cost, so it optimizes the true scalar rather than transaction size or write counts; its principal weakness is that prefix beam pruning and one-transaction relocations cannot jointly reverse a large set of interacting conflict directions. Build a MILP whose binary variables x[i,j] choose whether transaction i precedes transaction j for each relevant conflicting pair, with antisymmetry and transitivity/order-rank constraints. Reconstruct the operation precedence DAG implied by each transaction's internal operation chain and the selected read/write or write/write conflict directions, then introduce start-time variables and a makespan variable constrained by every precedence edge. Minimize that makespan directly using scipy.optimize.milp, and return transactions sorted by the solved integer ranks. Use the simulator only to verify the returned ordering and, if its exact semantics reveal a mismatch, add the missing precedence constraints rather than tuning heuristics. This is fundamentally stronger than beam search because it optimizes coupled conflict orientations globally instead of committing to them from partial prefixes.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The sole primary objective: the simulator makespan returned by workload.get_opt_seq_cost, and therefore the aggregate scalar score over the evaluator workloads.
active_paradigms.cautions: This requires inspecting txn_simulator semantics before encoding constraints: reads may conflict differently depending on whether the simulator uses locks, version dependencies, or transaction-level serialization. Do not include transitivity constraints for every triple on large instances unless necessary; use integer rank variables plus indicator/big-M constraints, or restrict pair variables to transaction pairs that actually share a key with at least one write. Big-M must safely exceed the longest possible operation schedule. Always preserve original transaction-internal operation order and convert ranks into a complete permutation with deterministic tie handling.

active_paradigms.idea: Use networkx.algorithms.components.strongly_connected_components to identify conflict-coupled scheduling cores and spend exact search budget only where order can matter
active_paradigms.description: The present search treats all transactions as equally coupled, samples only 24 candidates on large prefixes, and evaluates many relocations that may reverse no real read/write dependency. First construct a directed interaction representation from the workload: connect two transactions when they access a common key and at least one access is a write, while retaining per-key access information to distinguish actual conflict density. Apply networkx.algorithms.components.strongly_connected_components after orienting a provisional conflict graph from a simulator-scored seed order, so groups whose orientations mutually constrain one another become explicit hard cores. For each hard core small enough for exhaustive permutation search, enumerate its internal orders under fixed external boundary ranks and retain its simulator-best orientation; transactions outside such cores should be placed by their actual marginal simulator cost, not arbitrary beam-prefix survival. The key structural observation is that nonconflicting transactions cannot improve makespan through their relative order, whereas dense cores dominate the critical path and need joint moves much larger than the current three-transaction ruin. This can expose conflict clusters that the current random relocation search almost never flips simultaneously. Compare complete assembled schedules with workload.get_opt_seq_cost and retain only the actual best one.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Critical-path reductions caused by jointly changing the orientation of dense read/write conflict clusters, while avoiding simulator evaluations on independent or weakly coupled transaction pairs.
active_paradigms.cautions: A shared read-read key is not an edge and must not merge components. Strong components are a search-budget decomposition aid, not a proof that separately optimized component schedules compose optimally if the simulator has any global resource contention; final schedules must therefore always be rescored by get_opt_seq_cost. If an initial orientation makes the directed graph artificially acyclic, also consider undirected connected components as a conservative grouping fallback. Do not assume transaction IDs or textual operation lengths carry useful priority information.

active_paradigms.idea: Apply scipy.optimize.dual_annealing directly to a continuous random-key encoding of complete transaction permutations, scored exclusively by the simulator
active_paradigms.description: The current method is deterministic after one fixed seed and is dominated by local insertion neighborhoods; even its plateau moves change only one transaction at a time. Represent a candidate permutation by n continuous random keys, decode it as the transaction indices sorted by key, and define the objective as workload.get_opt_seq_cost of that decoded permutation. Call scipy.optimize.dual_annealing once with bounds [0,1] for every key and a fixed reproducible seed; this directly searches full permutations through occasional large coordinated rank changes rather than through beam-prefix commitments. Cache decoded permutations because many different key vectors induce the same ordering, and return the best decoded schedule observed by the objective. The simulator remains the objective oracle, so this method does not rely on an inaccurate proxy such as number of writes, graph degree, or operation count. Compared with the existing local search, annealing can cross high-cost intermediate schedules and reach an ordering basin requiring several conflict directions to change together. A modest polishing pass is unnecessary for the concept and should not replace the annealer's returned best schedule; the solver's best simulator-scored permutation is the output.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Escape from the local minima and equal-cost plateaus produced by relocation descent, seeking lower true simulator makespan through global coordinated permutation changes.
active_paradigms.cautions: Sorting random keys makes the objective piecewise constant with discontinuities, so configure a sufficiently high evaluation budget and use caching; it is a stochastic global discrete search, not a smooth continuous optimization claim. Bound cache memory as the current program does. Keep the seed fixed if evaluator consistency matters, and impose a time-aware maximum number of simulator evaluations because full schedule scoring may dominate runtime. For very small n, exhaustive enumeration remains preferable because it proves optimality.
